Zolotnyky Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopil Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Zolotnyky's cemetery was also used by the Jewish community of nearby Burkaniv. Jews are first mentioned in the town in 1533, and by the 16th century held more than half of its trading houses, stables, and taverns; the community later declined sharply under Austrian rule, from 225 people in 1890 to just 114 by 1921. Three rabbis served the community in succession: Fishl Malach in the 19th century, Zvi-Hirsch Schwartz in the 1920s, and Menachem-Mendl Mund in the 1930s.
